raw_response:
I have been working this land since I was a teenager. My father taught me, and his father taught him. I don't read books or go to training sessions, but I know this soil and this climate. Quzhou gets dry fast in spring and summer — my well is what keeps everything alive. Two of us in the house now, my wife and me. The children left for the city years ago.

My 34.5 mu is split the way I've always done it: about 20 mu for the wheat-maize rotation, and the rest — around 14-15 mu — for cotton. Cotton brings in more cash when the price is right, and I've been growing it long enough to handle it without hired labor most of the year.

For **wheat**, I'll plant in mid-October like always. I buy the improved seed from the village supply cooperative — same variety I've used for several years now, it does well here. I'll plough the field after maize harvest, apply compound fertilizer before seeding, then top-dress with urea around jointing stage. I irrigate at sowing, at jointing, and at heading — three times is usually enough if spring rains come. I spray once for weeds early on and once for aphids and rust near heading.

For **maize**, I plant right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste. I use hybrid seed, everyone in the village does now. I just scatter a bit of urea as topdress when the plant is knee-high, then again before tasseling. I'll water two or three times depending on rain. Maize doesn't need much from me, honestly. One spray for corn borer if it looks bad.

For **cotton**, this is the hard crop. I plant in late April after the last frost risk. Hybrid seed. Cotton needs me out there all summer — topping, spraying for bollworm, red spider mites, aphids. I'll spray at least six or seven times. I irrigate more carefully with cotton, maybe four times through the season. I split my fertilizer applications — some at transplanting, some as a sidedress when bolls are setting.

I don't plan to change much. What I've been doing feeds us and pays the bills. I'm 63 — I'm not experimenting.
